🧠 The AI Universe Is Much Bigger Than ChatGPT!
Most people think AI is just about asking questions and generating content.
But that's only the beginning. 👇
Artificial Intelligence is an entire ecosystem of technologies, and understanding how they connect can change the way you learn, build, and work.
Here's a breakdown of the AI universe and how its major technologies fit together.
1. Artificial Intelligence (AI)
AI is the broad field of creating systems that can perform tasks that typically require human intelligence.
It includes reasoning, planning, language understanding, computer vision, robotics, and decision-making.
2. Machine Learning (ML)
Machine learning enables computers to learn patterns from data instead of relying entirely on explicitly programmed rules.
It's used in recommendations, fraud detection, prediction, classification, and countless everyday applications.
3. Neural Networks
Neural networks are computing systems inspired by the way biological neurons process information.
They help machines recognize complex patterns, process images, understand language, and make predictions.
4. Deep Learning
Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn increasingly complex patterns from large amounts of data.
It's one of the key technologies behind modern speech recognition, image generation, advanced language models, and autonomous systems.
5. Generative AI
Generative AI takes things even further.
Instead of simply analyzing existing information, it can generate new content, including text, images, audio, video, and code.
Tools powered by generative AI are already transforming content creation, software development, research, and business workflows.
6. Transformers and Large Language Models
Transformers are a neural network architecture that has become fundamental to many modern AI systems.
They help models process relationships between elements in sequences, making them especially effective for language-related tasks.
Large language models use these capabilities to summarize information, answer questions, write content, and assist with complex tasks.
7. The Technologies Behind the Scenes
The AI universe also includes technologies such as:
Natural Language Processing (NLP)
Computer Vision
Reinforcement Learning
Transfer Learning
Robotics
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
AI Agents
Multimodal AI
Each technology solves different problems, and many modern AI products combine several of them to deliver more powerful results.
Here's the biggest takeaway:
You don't need to master every branch of AI to benefit from it.
Start by understanding the fundamentals, explore the tools relevant to your goals, and learn how to apply them to real-world problems.
The people who learn to use AI effectively won't just save time. They'll discover entirely new ways to create, solve problems, and build opportunities.
AI is not one technology. It's an entire universe of possibilities. 🚀
The real question is: How will you use it?

A robot's movement can teach us more than you might think. 🤖

Imagine controlling a robot arm on your computer screen.

You move it toward an object, adjust its position, and try to pick it up. Every movement is part of the task.

Now imagine those actions being recorded as data that can help train robots.

That's the interesting idea behind simulation-based robot training.

With @axisrobotics Robotics, people can interact with simulated robots and demonstrate how different tasks should be performed.

These demonstrations can be captured as trajectories basically, records of how the robot moved while completing a task.

Why does that matter?

Because robots need examples of how to perform physical actions. 
Human demonstrations can provide useful training data without requiring every contributor to own a physical robot.

Of course, a simulation isn't the same as the real world. Robots still need to handle unexpected situations and be tested outside virtual environments.

But making robot training more accessible could open the door for more people to contribute to the future of physical AI.

Sometimes, teaching a robot starts with something as simple as showing it how a task is done. 🦾

We’re sharing more of our research, starting with our paper on outcome-routed post-training for diffusion language models.

Many standard RL methods are difficult to apply reliably to diffusion language models. Our approach avoids policy likelihood ratios and combines reward-based learning with teacher guidance.

Tool-calling accuracy (BFCL) rose from 53.55% to 88.6%, without increasing the model’s size.

The result: a more effective way to post train diffusion language models for new capabilities.

Our team will present the work at the NeurIPS 2026 DiffuLM. https://t.co/zTjk2to0hm

Diffusion models are complicated to RL because many training methods that work for AR don't work well for diffusion.

We present a methodology for post-training diffusion models that combines reward-based learning with teacher guidance.

The result is more effective way to post train diffusion language models for new capabilities.
